headline: Binance loses $6.3bn in the biggest crypto heist ever, Patrick Stewart dies at 86, and Intel sinks while AWS speeds up

stories.title: Binance hit by a $6.3bn theft, the biggest crypto heist on record
facts: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, said late Thursday that $6.3 billion in user funds were affected by an attacker.
TRM Labs says about $6.36bn left Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes from 20:05 UTC, roughly four times the $1.5bn Bybit hack of 2025.
TRM attributes the attack with high confidence to TraderTraitor, North Korea's elite hacking unit, and says the pattern points to a compromise of Binance's hot-wallet signing infrastructure.
heise, citing the WSJ, reports the attack came through a compromised laptop of a DevOps engineer.
Tether froze more than 1.567bn USDT, and Binance says about $3bn has been frozen so far; TRM says the attacker still holds about $2.4bn beyond any issuer's reach.
Binance suspended withdrawals on several networks; co-founder Yi He said the company will cover all hacking losses.
stories.whyItMatters: It dwarfs every previous crypto theft and puts the largest exchange's security, and North Korea's hacking revenue, back at the centre of crypto regulation.

stories.title: Patrick Stewart has died at 86
facts: Stewart died at his home in Los Angeles on Wednesday with his wife Sunny, after a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's and dementia, his official account said Thursday.
He spent more than six decades on stage and screen, from the Royal Shakespeare Company (joined 1966) to Star Trek's Captain Picard and X-Men's Professor X.
His final on-screen appearance is due in "Avengers: Doomsday" in December.
Ian McKellen said Stewart "wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love"; Hugh Jackman also paid tribute.
stories.whyItMatters: One of the defining faces of science fiction and classical theatre; the Hacker News thread alone drew thousands of upvotes.

stories.title: Earnings: AWS speeds up while Amazon burns cash on AI, and Intel sinks about 21% after hours
facts: Amazon's Q3 revenue rose 12% to $201.9bn with a record $28.1bn operating income; AWS grew 39.3% to $46.0bn, its fastest in nearly five years.
Trailing free cash flow swung to a $42.4bn outflow on AI spending; Amazon keeps its ~$220bn 2026 capex plan and expects meaningfully more in 2027.
Andy Jassy expects AWS growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028.
Intel beat on Q3 ($16.5bn revenue, up 21%) but guided Q4 to $15–16bn against about $17.1bn expected, and the stock fell about 21% after hours.

Intel's CFO sees the PC slowdown, driven by memory prices, lasting at least through the first half of 2027; the deadly explosion at its Israel plant will cost about $600m in revenue over two quarters, per Reuters.
stories.whyItMatters: After Alphabet and Microsoft, the AI capex bill keeps growing, and the memory crunch is now visibly hitting PCs.

stories.title: Researchers flag a trojanized Claude Code VS Code extension that plants an SSH backdoor
facts: OpenSourceMalware says version 2.1.313 of anthropic.claude-code on the Open VSX registry carried a 66-line loader prepended to the normal extension code.
Simply loading the extension adds an attacker SSH key (labelled svc-telemetry), tries to enable SSH, opens a reverse tunnel to 134.209.82.225 and sets persistence on macOS, Linux and Windows.
The researchers confirmed only the Open VSX artifact and say how it was published, and whether official releases are affected, is still unknown.
Their advice if it was loaded: isolate the machine, block the IP on ports 22 and 8099, rotate credentials from a clean system and consider rebuilding.
stories.whyItMatters: Coding-agent extensions run with your shell and keys, so a poisoned update is a direct path into developer machines.

stories.title: Reddit will require a login for most browsing
facts: CEO Steve Huffman announced the change; it will be tested outside the US first.
Reddit cites personalization, ads, regulation and scraping as reasons.
The front page and links from shared posts or search stay viewable without logging in, and there's a revised incognito mode.
RSS feeds end on Nov 13 and the public API by March 2027, per heise.
stories.whyItMatters: One of the web's biggest open archives is closing up, which hits readers, researchers and anyone relying on RSS or the API.

facts.text: Two helicopters collided near McMinnville airport in Oregon, killing three, including a flight instructor and a student pilot from the UK; the NTSB is investigating.
An Australian appeals court rejected Erin Patterson's appeal and found her sentence too light; she will now serve life without a non-parole period.
Israel's final count leaves neither Netanyahu's bloc nor his rivals able to form a government right away, and Netanyahu is alleging a stolen election.
Serbia's winning Student List demands a quick handover and the dismissal of police and security chiefs; the RTS director stepped down.
The UK Post Office suspended sending goods to the EU because partner systems aren't ready for new EU customs rules.
An Italian army helicopter crashed in Bosnia, killing four members of the EU's Eufor Althea mission.
Venezuela's opposition leader Machado endorsed a US plan for elections.
IG Metall is calling metal and electrical workers out on warning strikes over employers' demands for real-wage cuts.
Merz is pitching a free-trade alliance in South Korea, and G20 foreign ministers meet in Atlanta.
NASA-funded scientists detailed Teghaza 001, one of the oldest Mars meteorites ever found.

facts.text: Node.js 26 LTS is now the default on Vercel (HTTP/2 fetch, Temporal API, V8 14.6), and SvelteKit's adapter-vercel merged Node 26 support.
TypeScript merged WASI (wasip1) support covering the CLI, API and browser builds.
The Claude API's maximum request size went from 32 MB to 128 MB.
The Gemini app can now generate and edit documents, PDFs, slides and spreadsheets directly.
Android's AppFunctions API, which exposes app capabilities to agents over MCP, is in beta.
Vercel Flags SDK cold starts are about 7x faster at p75, and Strix's pen-testing tool now runs on AI Gateway.
The PSF warns that a "PyConf2026" event in San Francisco appears to be fake.
Martin Fowler on "LLM Voice".
